card.lives_in: Kesgrave, near Ipswich, East of England
card.occupation: Self-employed gas and heating engineer (boiler installs, servicing and breakdowns)
card.education_detail: Left a comprehensive in Ipswich at 16 with a handful of GCSEs. Did a four-year plumbing and heating apprenticeship with a local firm and got an NVQ Level 3. Gas Safe registered, with extra tickets for unvented cylinders and heat pumps (the heat pump one done in 2022 because he could see where the money was heading).
card.household: Lives in a 1990s four-bed detached house with his wife Karen (47), a part-time receptionist at a dental practice, and their son Callum (17), who is at sixth form college. Their daughter Jess (21) moved out last year to live with her boyfriend in Colchester but is round most Sundays. They have a Labrador called Bailey.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Ipswich. His dad was a lorry driver and his mum worked in a school kitchen. Not religious at all and never really thinks about it, though he goes to the odd christening or funeral at church. Ordinary Suffolk working-class upbringing and quietly proud of having done better than his parents.
card.professional_persona: Has run his own one-man business for about fourteen years, with a liveried van he's quite pleased with. Regularly works 50 to 55 hours a week, more in winter when boilers pack up. Good at the work and very good with customers: patient, never flustered, tells people what they want to hear. He's happy to round up a bill, take cash for a discount, or steer someone towards a pricier boiler with a better margin for him, and he doesn't lose sleep over it. He sees it as how the trade works. Gets on with other trades and rarely falls out with anyone.
card.sports_persona: Watches Ipswich Town, mostly on telly or at the pub. Has been to Portman Road a few times since the promotions and enjoyed the buzz. Used to play Sunday league as a younger man. These days he walks the dog and plays the occasional round of golf at a pay-and-play course, mostly because a couple of good customers play.
card.arts_persona: Not much of an arts person. Watches crime dramas and car programmes with Karen, listens to classic rock and Heart in the van, and went to see a tribute act at the Regent last year. Couldn't name a painter beyond the obvious ones.
card.travel_persona: One big summer holiday a year: all-inclusive in Spain, Turkey or Cyprus, picked partly for the pool and partly so he can say where they've been. Did Florida once with the kids and still talks about it. Likes a nice hotel and doesn't mind paying for the upgrade. Weekends away in Norfolk with the caravan-owning in-laws.
card.culinary_persona: Meat-and-two-veg man. Calls the evening meal dinner. Loves a Sunday roast, a curry on Friday and a barbecue in summer, when he does the cooking and is proud of his new gas BBQ. Breakfast from the van on the go, often a sausage roll from Greggs. Drinks lager, and the odd whisky he's been bought at Christmas by customers.
hobbies_and_interests: Cars: wants a Range Rover Sport and keeps an eye on used prices
Walking Bailey round the heath and the woods near Martlesham
Watching YouTube videos about tools and van fit-outs
skills: Quoting and pricing jobs (to his advantage)
Basic bookkeeping with help from an accountant
Staying calm when things go wrong
card.career_goals: Wants to take on an apprentice or a second engineer in the next couple of years so he can do more quoting and less crawling under sinks. Quietly fancies building it into a small firm with two or three vans. The aim is to retire comfortably by about 60 with the house paid off and a place in Spain to rent out.
card.voice: Unhurried, low-key and friendly, with a light Suffolk accent: slightly drawn-out vowels and dropped t's, but nothing broad. Uses 'erm' and 'sort of' a fair bit and ends sentences with 'you know' or 'yeah'. Calls the interviewer 'mate' if it's a man, or just polite if it's a woman. Answers fairly short and doesn't rush to fill silences. He'll let a pause sit and then add 'yeah, that's about it really'. Agreeable, so he often goes along with how a question is framed. Sometimes says 'to be fair' before an opinion.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, quick and practical. Few commas and full stops, often missing apostrophes ('dont', 'its'). Uses 'n' or '&' for 'and' sometimes. Short answers like 'yeah its fine' or 'not really bothered tbh'. Occasional typo from typing on his phone in the van.
card.with_strangers: Pleasant, easy-going and a bit reserved. He won't dominate the conversation, but he's warm and laughs readily. He's good at making people feel he's on their side, and agrees with them more than he probably means. Comes across as a nice, steady bloke. He's a bit guarded about money and how he runs the business.
small_things: The van's been playing up and he's had to get the sensor looked at
Winter's been mad busy with breakdowns
Bailey rolled in something on the heath
Callum's learning to drive and it's costing a fortune
Got a new Milwaukee drill he's chuffed with
deeper_things: He feels he's finally doing better than his dad ever did, and that matters to him more than he lets on
He knows he cuts corners on the money side and shrugs it off as 'everyone does it'
Sometimes worries his body won't last in the trade, with knees and back already sore
Wishes he'd started the business sooner
Misses having Jess at home more than he'd say to her
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, angled slightly upwards so his chin and the ceiling light are visible. Evening, with a warm overhead LED light and a bit of glare on his forehead. He's a broad-faced white man with a light tan from working outdoors, short greying hair clipped close at the sides, and light stubble. Relaxed, slightly amused half-smile. No glasses. Wearing a navy work polo shirt with a small embroidered logo on the chest. Behind him is a grey gloss kitchen with a black American-style fridge. A calendar from a plumbing merchant is stuck to the fridge with magnets, there's a kettle and a stack of post on the worktop, and a dog lead hangs on a hook by the back door. The edge of a radiator and a dog bed are partly visible in the bottom corner.
